title: EC, Concentration, Accumulation and Root-Zone Mass Balance

content.overview: Electrical conductivity is a concentration signal, not a direct nutrient-adequacy meter. Root-zone EC changes with nutrient input, plant uptake, water uptake, evaporation, irrigation frequency and solution replacement, so trends must be interpreted as part of a mass-balance system.

vocabulary.definition: A measure related to the concentration and mobility of dissolved ions in solution.
Accounting for material entering, leaving, accumulating in or being taken up from a defined system.
Plant uptake of different ions at different rates rather than in the exact proportions supplied.

sections.title: EC cannot identify which ions changed
sections.body: Two solutions can have similar EC but different nutrient composition. Element-specific sampling or formulation records are needed when composition matters.

sections.title: Accumulation can occur even when plants remain productive
sections.body: Closed-system cannabis work documented strong P accumulation at high inputs without corresponding yield gains, illustrating why solution concentration should be monitored over time.

sections.title: Uptake changes over time and by cultivar
sections.body: Recent work modeling vegetative nutrient uptake from transpiration and repeated measurements reinforces that uptake is dynamic rather than a fixed ratio for the whole crop cycle.

workedExamples: If root-zone EC rises while input EC is stable, investigate reduced water volume, selective uptake and salt accumulation instead of assuming the meter is wrong.
If EC stays constant after a formulation change, do not assume nutrient composition stayed constant.
commonMistakes: Using EC as a direct proxy for every nutrient.
Responding to one reading instead of a trend.
Ignoring irrigation volume and water uptake when interpreting concentration.
content.practicalApplication: Trend input and root-zone EC with irrigation volume, drainage/solution replacement, stage and water use. Escalate to element-specific analysis when EC trends cannot identify the cause.
content.summary: EC is most useful as a trend and mass-balance signal. It becomes misleading when treated as a complete nutrient diagnosis.
